title: The Impact of Social Nudges on User-Generated Content for Social Network Platforms
eligible_reason: Randomized field experiment on a video-sharing platform ('Platform O'): providers are randomly assigned to receive social nudges (treatment vs control), and almost every regression is a cross-sectional OLS of a provider-level outcome on the treatment indicator (sm.OLS 'y ~ 1 + treatment', Tables 2-13, 15, 17-21). The only pre/post designs are two-period comparisons: Table 14 column 1 (control-group providers, whether_follower_send_author_msg_exp_time x post, day before the experiment vs the first reception day, clustered by author) and Table 16 (matched like/comment users, treatment x post, two periods). There is no staggered binary adoption, no unit or calendar-time fixed effects, and no event study.
design_notes: Empirical_Analyses.py (statsmodels, Jupyter export) and Simulation_Analyses.py (network model, Section 6). Code reads social_nudge_first_exp_*.csv, social_nudge_second_exp_production_diffusion.csv, platform_nudge_production.csv, social_nudge_first_exp_control_group_did.csv and social_nudge_first_exp_like_comment_cannibalize_data.csv; none of these files is in the package. Table 14 col 1 (line 1167): photo_id_cnt_fillzero ~ whether_follower_send_author_msg_exp_time*post, cluster author_id. Table 16 (lines 1483-1486): sending_like_cnt / sending_comment_cnt ~ treatment*post on a matched user sample.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: No staggered adoption: random assignment, outcomes measured on each provider's first reception day.
data_files_note: Social_Nudge_MS_Data_Readme.pdf gives a data dictionary, but no CSV used by Empirical_Analyses.py is shipped; only distributional summaries are included.
priority_note: RCT without staggered adoption; data not shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Ruled out on design: randomized experiment with provider-level ATE regressions; the full-text 'difference-in-differences' hit refers to the two-period Table 14/16 comparisons.
